segment.description: Hiwassee River trout tailwater (Apalachia release water), Polk County - the powerhouse release through Reliance
segment.boundaries: Catalog entry says 'Appalachia Dam release water at the NC line through Reliance to the Chickamauga Lake head'; research shows the cold trout water begins at Apalachia POWERHOUSE - a pipeline/tunnel carries release water ~8.3 miles downstream from the dam, so the first ~10 miles of riverbed below the dam are bypassed and are not the trout water (TVA; TU Hiwassee chapter). Reliance is the mid-reach trout anchor; the lower reach warms toward the Chickamauga Lake head.

damTailwater.dam: Apalachia Dam (release via pipeline/tunnel to Apalachia Powerhouse)

coldSource.notes: TVA describes Apalachia Reservoir as 'a small, deep, cool-water reservoir' whose water is carried ~8.3 miles by pipeline/tunnel to the powerhouse - i.e. deep (cold) source water for the trout reach. USGS 03556590 (Hiwassee River above Reliance, ~759 ft elevation) is the correct trout-reach gauge; catalog's other gauge 03566000 is Hiwassee River AT CHARLESTON, far downstream near the Chickamauga head - wrong reach for trout temperatures (verified via USGS site catalog).

holdover.detail: No agency survival figure found in this pass. The delayed-harvest program (stocked Feb/Oct/Nov per TWRA workbook, catch-and-release Oct 1-Feb 28) structurally requires multi-month carry-over of stocked fish from fall to spring, but no published Hiwassee-specific holdover estimate was located.

wildPopulation.detail: TVA's tailwater trout page says cold releases support trout 'including natural (wild) reproduction' in some TVA tailwaters, but no Hiwassee-specific age-0 survey or agency reproduction statement was found. TU's Hiwassee chapter describes the fishery as stocked (not native). TWRA Region IV reports not verified in this pass.

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: Cold deep-source tunnel releases sustain the trout reach, but the Reliance gauge hit 23.8 C on 27 July 2025 with 11 days at or above 22 C that month - summer is survivable but marginal in low water.
